cues.text: Three shots. Cover, frame one, host and dialog box hidden: the dispatch board, our service area with 14 red pins already down (the 14 missed calls), the hero "14" big in gold, plate "14 missed calls." / "Need an AI receptionist?", chip "PART 1 OF 2", EXAMPLE tag. By 0.8 s cut in close: a desk phone on the dash, its screen MISSED CALL with the red badge "14"; Snow and the dialog box come in. On "Need" cut to the third shot: a laptop on a desk, AI RECEPTIONIST on its screen with a talking wave; the plate stays up.
Our own office: the laptop's demo screen big (AI RECEPTIONIST, DEMO, the wave moving), "PART 1 OF 2: THE COUNT" on the card above it.
Gold stars pop over the wave on "great"; on "sign" a quote sheet slides up with a pen and a SIGN HERE line.
Cut to the dispatch board again, the 14 red pins; plate "14 missed calls." / "Worth how much?"; a red stamp "WORTH: ?" hits on "worth"; Snow shrugs.
The calendar set, NOVEMBER: a red X lands on each day from 1 to 14 on "mark every call"; the gold week strip sits on week 1, then week 2. Line in the strip under it: "Mark every missed call."
Four of the days take a gold coin, one by one ("real jobs"). The strip line turns to "Circle the real jobs."
"4 JOBS OF 14 CALLS" lands in the strip, EXAMPLE tag.
Our own chalk board, EXAMPLE: "4 jobs x what you clear" chalks on.
"$350" lands in place of "what you clear": "4 x $350".
"= $1,400" hero size, "in 2 weeks" under it; held.
"x 2: call it $2,800 a month" chalks under it; the whole board held.
A balance scale on the office desk: the left pan "$2,800 / MO" (missed jobs), the right pan the quote sheet "QUOTE / MO".
The quote pan drops; red stamp "NOT PAID BACK YET".
The pan swings up; teal "TRY PART 2".
The inventory set, title "PART 2": three slots, TEXT BACK, A PERSON, AI; the cursor jumps slot to slot on "three options side by side".

Back on the chalk board, a tally of 14 strokes chalked in the corner; the rule lands big: "Count the" / "missed calls" (gold) / "before you buy.", "NEXT: PART 2" under it. Snow waves. Then the end card with the send line: "Send this to whoever signs the software bills."
